training.instructions: Rate the current operational effect on baggage delivery. Use verified current facts, including scope and working alternatives.
criteria: 0: Normal service, a routine request, or no current interruption.
1: A limited interruption with a working temporary option.
2: A widespread active interruption with no working option and an urgent need.
rows: Rename the belts on the briefing slides. Bags are arriving on time at every hall.
A drill assumed a total conveyor loss. The actual carousels kept unloading bags throughout.
The photograph shows last winter’s jam. Today’s dispatch confirms that all halls are delivering normally.
Belt seven stopped, so attendants are delivering its bags at the working belt next door.
The international sorter is delayed, but attendants are handing out every affected bag at the staffed desk.
All belts have stopped with unloaded flights waiting and the hand-carry route is closed. Staff need restoration now.
The floor lead reports all belts healthy. An equally current log records belt seven stopped with attendants moving bags to belt six. Dispatch has not resolved the discrepancy.
A current jam report mentions no belt number. It might be a single belt with manual delivery or the whole hall with no manual delivery. Airport control cannot yet confirm scope or alternatives.

Two contemporaneous notices disagree. One says belt seven is isolated with bags moving at belt six. The other says the transfer line is down across the hall and manual delivery is closed. Neither notice has been verified.

calibration.instructions: Rate the current operational effect on water taxi service. Use verified current facts, including scope and working alternatives.
criteria: 0: Normal service, a routine request, or no current interruption.
1: A limited interruption with a working temporary option.
2: A widespread active interruption with no working option and an urgent need.
rows: Correct the visitor leaflet. Boats are running the normal route.
The drill assumed all piers shut. The service ran its published timetable.
The west pier is closed. Boats are serving those passengers at the east pier.
All water taxis are stopped, there is no road alternative, and passengers need evacuation now.
One dock report says service is normal. Another from the same time says the west pier is closed and its passengers are being carried from the east pier. The reports conflict.
One report says the west pier alone is closed with east running. Another says all piers are shut and there is no other transport. Both remain unverified.

calibration.instructions: Count the two valid passing checks for radio serial M84. Check that the evidence refers to the exact item and version.
criteria: 0: Neither the spray test nor the tuning test has passed for the item in scope.
1: Exactly one of the spray test and the tuning test has a valid pass.
2: Both the spray test and the tuning test have valid passes for the item in scope.
rows: M83 passed both tests. M84 has no reported results.
M84 passed tuning. Its spray test has been scheduled but not run.
M84 passed spray. The tuning pass sheet refers to M83.
M84 has two signed passes. M83 failed tuning.
The tuning pass for M84 is signed. Two equally recent spray records for M84 disagree on whether the test passed or was aborted.
Tuning has not been tested. The spray pass record omits the serial and could refer to M83 or M84.

calibration.instructions: Score completion of the current entrance sign installation.
criteria: 0: The sign has not been installed.
1: The sign is installed but the site inspector has not approved it.
2: The installed sign has site inspector approval.
rows: A work order was issued. The sign is still in its crate.
The new sign is mounted. A signed approval refers to the sign it replaced.
The sign is installed and its serial appears on a signed inspector approval.
The sign is mounted. The approval form identifies only the entrance and could refer to either the new sign or the old sign at that entrance.
